problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $4{x}^{2}-9{y}^{2}-32x+18y+19=0.$

activity_context.topic_title: Asymptotes of Hyperbolas Centered at a General Point

feedback.problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola ${x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+8x+7=0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+8x+7 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+8x-{y}^{2}+7 & =0 \\ (x+4)^{2}-16-{y}^{2}+7 & =0 \\ (x+4)^{2}-{y}^{2}-9 & =0 \\ (x+4)^{2}-{y}^{2} & =9 \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

The standard equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a horizontal hyperbola, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y-k=\pm \frac{b}{a}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
(h,k)=(-4,0),\,a=\sqrt{9}=3,\,b=\sqrt{9}=3.
$$

 

Therefore, the asymptotes are given by

$$
y=\pm (x+4).
$$
